recipe_steps: Wash the apples well.
Slice into wedges, removing the core.
Serve chilled.
Peel the bananas.
Serve whole or sliced.
Mash the bananas and preheat the oven to 175°C.
Whisk eggs and sugar until pale, then mix in the melted butter and mashed banana.
Fold in the flour and baking powder until just combined.
Pour into a lined tin and bake 40–45 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool before slicing.
Rinse the barley and add to a pot with the water and pandan leaves.
Bring to a boil, then simmer 40–45 minutes until the barley is soft.
Add rock sugar to taste and stir to dissolve.
Serve warm or chilled.
Preheat oven to 175°C and line a square tin.
Melt the chocolate and butter together and let cool slightly.
Whisk eggs and sugar, then stir in the chocolate mixture.
Fold in flour and cocoa until just combined.
Bake 25–30 minutes until the top is set but the centre is still fudgy.
Cool before cutting into squares.
Wash and peel the oranges.
Separate into segments and serve.
Peel and roughly chop the guava.
Blend with water until smooth.
Strain out the seeds.
Sweeten to taste, add a squeeze of lime, and serve over ice.
Soak the mung beans for a few hours, then drain.
Boil with pandan and ginger until the beans are soft and split, about 30–40 minutes.
Add palm sugar and a pinch of salt and stir to dissolve.
Pour in the coconut milk and warm through without boiling hard.
Serve warm.
Wash the pears.
Slice into wedges and serve chilled.
Peel the papaya and scoop out the seeds.
Cut into cubes and serve chilled.
Spoon the yogurt into bowls.
Top with fresh fruit and a drizzle of honey.
Blanch the pork ribs in boiling water, then drain and rinse.
Add the ribs to a pot with water, whole garlic, cracked peppercorns and the spice packet.
Bring to a boil, then simmer covered for about 1.5 hours until tender.
Season with light and dark soy sauce.
Serve hot with rice.
Fry minced garlic in a little oil until fragrant, then add the stock.
Bring to a boil and add the fish balls and cubed tofu.
Simmer a few minutes until everything is heated through.
Season with salt and white pepper.
Finish with sliced spring onion and serve.

Blanch the pork bones, rinse, then simmer with the beans in fresh water.
Add garlic, onion and tomato and simmer until the beans are soft, about 1 hour.
Season with salt and serve hot.
Soak the peanuts for an hour, then drain.
Blanch and rinse the pork bones.
Simmer the peanuts and bones together until soft, about 1–1.5 hours.
Season with garlic and salt and serve.

Add chunked potatoes, carrots and onion.
Simmer until the vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and pepper, finish with spring onion, and serve.

Add chunked daikon and carrot.

Season with salt and white pepper and serve.
Bring the stock to a boil with smashed garlic.

Season with salt and serve immediately.

Season lightly with salt and serve.
Bring the stock to a boil with smashed garlic.
Add the greens and cook briefly.
Stream in the beaten eggs while stirring gently.
Season with salt and pepper and serve.

Arrange all the raw ingredients on platters around the pot.
Cook meats, seafood and balls in the broth until done.
Add vegetables and tofu towards the end.
Serve with dipping sauces.
Bring the stock and creamed corn to a simmer.
Add the crab meat.

Stream in the egg whites while stirring to form ribbons.
Season with white pepper and serve hot.

Add the meatballs and simmer until cooked.

Coat in beaten egg, then toss in cornstarch.

Clean the baby squid.
Blend shallots, garlic and chilies into a coarse paste.
Fry the paste until fragrant, then add tomato.

Season with kecap manis, salt and sugar, and serve.
Pat the squid rings dry and season with salt, pepper and garlic powder.
Toss in cornstarch to coat.
Deep-fry in hot oil for a minute or two until golden.
Drain and serve with a squeeze of lime.
Tear the mushrooms into strips.
Mix the flours with garlic powder, salt and pepper.

Deep-fry until golden and crisp, then drain.

Blend shallots, garlic and chilies into a coarse sambal.
Fry the sambal until fragrant and the raw smell is gone.
Season with palm sugar and tamarind.
Toss in the fried tempe and anchovies to coat, and serve.

Rest, then slice into pieces and serve.

Sprinkle with a little salt.
Deep-fry in hot oil until golden and crisp on the outside.
Drain and serve with chili or sweet soy dip.

Grind garlic, coriander and salt with a little water into a marinade.
Soak the tempe slices in the marinade briefly.
Deep-fry until golden and crisp, then drain.
Rinse and dry the anchovies well.

Briefly fry sliced garlic and chili, add a pinch of sugar.
Toss the crispy anchovies through and serve.
Fry the julienned ginger and garlic in oil until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir-fry until it changes colour.
Season with oyster sauce and a splash of water; simmer until cooked.
Finish with spring onion and sesame oil, and serve.
Fry sliced garlic and shallots until fragrant.
Add the spinach and stir-fry over high heat until just wilted.
Season with oyster sauce and salt, and serve immediately.
